library_supplier_contracts.contract: Finite-dimensional vector Brownian motion starts at zero, has independent N_d(0,(t-s)I_d) increments, continuous paths on one full event; coordinates are independent Brownian random elements. The definition itself includes no filtration.
Scalar predictable square-integrable integrands are defined by L2 limits of elementary predictable integrals; this definition alone does not assert linearity or path properties.
For finite-energy scalar predictable H,K, the Ito map is linear and isometric in predictable L2; cross identity holds. Vector/matrix integrals must be built from finite coordinate sums.

For a continuous d-dimensional Brownian Ito process and f in C^{1,2}, the drift correction uses (σσ^T)^{ij}/2 and the stochastic term is the finite coordinate sum; the displayed process is assumed to have the stated usual-filtration integrability conditions.

findings: Anderson’s theorem/proof was read in full over PDF pp. 1–9. The exact theorem is density-based: a.s.-bounded initial state independent of forward Brownian motion, a unique smooth forward density, and unique smooth augmented joint and conditional joint densities.

The reverse driver is constructed from the score-weighted derivative of pσ, then shown to have increments independent of X_t in the decreasing filtration. Reparameterizing s=T−t yields −b+div(a)+a∇log p, with div(a)_i=Σ_j ∂_j a_ij.
Strong SDE existence by itself does not imply any density/joint-KFP hypotheses. Singular initial laws require application on positive smoothing times and a separately justified weak endpoint limit.
